governance.status: LEVEL 2 — TECHNICALLY VERIFIED, NOT EXTERNALLY ATTESTED
governance.description: Transfer Hypotheses Portfolio: Detailed transfer records with literature precedents, structural match analysis, falsification experiments, and verdicts.

hypotheses.name: ETD / Integrating Factor Integrator for Stiff Semilinear PDEs
hypotheses.original_failure: Full-state turbulent ROM accuracy plateaued at moderate ranks due to modal truncation of high-frequency turbulent cascade, NOT due to integrator instability.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Exact machine-precision integration of stiff linear diffusion operator via diagonal integrating factor exp(-nu * lambda_k * dt), removing diffusive CFL stability constraint.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Stiff semilinear reaction-diffusion equations (Fisher-KPP, Allen-Cahn, Gierer-Meinhardt pattern formation)
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Identical operator splitting: u_t = D * Lap(u) + R(u) where D*Lap is diagonal in Laplacian eigenbasis and R(u) is non-stiff polynomial reaction kinetics)
hypotheses.literature_precedent: ESTABLISHED (Kassam & Trefethen 2005, SIAM J. Sci. Comput.; Hochbruck & Ostermann 2010, Acta Numerica)
hypotheses.novelty: ALREADY STANDARD (Known standard method; high-confidence direct transfer)
hypotheses.important_differences: Reaction kinetics R(u) are local polynomials (e.g. u(1-u) or u - u^3), which are computationally cheaper than fluid advection (u·∇)u.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: The linear diffusion part is solved analytically without time-step restriction; explicit Runge-Kutta stepping of polynomial kinetics is unconditionally stable for reasonable reaction timescales.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: If reaction kinetics become extremely stiff (very fast chemical reaction rates), explicit RK stepping of the reaction term could limit the timestep, requiring IMEX or full exponential Rosenbrock schemes.
hypotheses.code_reuse: DIRECT (Reuses IntegratingFactorModalODEIntegrator class with replaced RHS callback)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Simulate 1D Allen-Cahn equation u_t = epsilon * u_xx + u(1 - u^2) on [0, 2*pi] with epsilon=0.01 at dt=0.05. If integrator exhibits numerical instability or blows up compared to Crank-Nicolson, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Proves whether our ETD implementation maintains unconditional diffusive stability and 4th-order accuracy on non-fluid reaction-diffusion benchmarks.

hypotheses.name: Stokes / Laplacian Geometry Eigenbasis for Parametric Heat Conduction & Thermal Transients
hypotheses.original_failure: Stokes eigenmodes had slow convergence on turbulent nonlinear velocity fluctuations because Navier-Stokes convection (u·∇)u couples modes across all scales.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Exact analytical Laplacian eigenfunction expansion satisfying inhomogeneous boundary conditions (no-slip / Dirichlet / Neumann) on fixed 3D Cartesian domains.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Linear parabolic heat conduction u_t = alpha * Lap(u) + Q(x,t) with fixed wall boundary conditions and time-varying heat sources.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Exact mathematical identity: heat equation on a fixed domain is completely diagonalized by the Laplacian eigenbasis, reducing PDE to uncoupled 1D scalar ODEs a_k'(t) = -alpha * lambda_k * a_k(t) + q_k(t)).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: ESTABLISHED (Classical Fourier-Bessel spectral theory; Quarteroni, Manzoni, Negri 2015, Reduced Basis Methods)
hypotheses.novelty: ALREADY STANDARD (Classical technique; serves as a zero-risk implementation verification baseline)
hypotheses.important_differences: Zero nonlinear advection; solution is fully uncoupled in modal space; energy decay is strictly monotonic.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: The Stokes eigenmodes computed by our codebase ARE the exact discrete eigenfunctions of the staggered-grid Laplacian. In the absence of convection, projection error decays exponentially with mode index for smooth initial thermal fields.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: Only if boundary condition stencils on the MAC staggered grid introduce unexpected flux leakage for scalar fields (which is prevented by our ScalarField ghost padding).
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Run 3D unsteady heat conduction with localized Gaussian thermal pulse in channel geometry. Measure relative L2 error vs analytical series solution. If error > 1e-10 at rank r=100, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Validates exact mathematical correctness of our basis generator and establishes machine-precision baseline on purely linear PDEs.

hypotheses.name: Resolvent Input-Output Analysis for Boundary-Actuated Wall Shear Control
hypotheses.original_failure: Discarded in W9 because computing dense SVD of resolvent operators at all wavenumber pairs was too computationally expensive for a full-state time-stepping ROM, and speedup dropped to 0.95x.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Singular value decomposition of the linearized Navier-Stokes resolvent operator identifies optimal directional forcing modes that produce maximum wall shear stress response.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Active turbulent drag reduction via boundary wall blowing/suction or opposition control in channel flows.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Resolvent operator (i*omega*I - L)^(-1) is the exact transfer function from actuator forcing to wall shear stress observable).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (McKeon & Sharma 2010, J. Fluid Mech.; Toedtli, Luhar, McKeon 2019, Phys. Rev. Fluids; Brunton & Noack 2015, Appl. Mech. Rev.)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN COMPONENTS / NEW COMBINATION (Adapting our discrete MAC-staggered resolvent SVD to output-specific wall shear control rather than full-state Galerkin expansion)
hypotheses.important_differences: Target observable is 1D wall shear stress tau_w(x,z) at the boundary, NOT the 3D internal velocity field u(x,y,z). SVD only needs to be computed for targeted actuation frequencies omega and actuation wavenumbers (kx, kz).
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: Turbulent wall shear stress is dominated by low-rank, highly amplified response modes (rank-1 approximation captures >80% of boundary response gain). Targeting the boundary observable avoids the full-state Kolmogorov dimension barrier.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: Linearized resolvent gain predictions may degrade if nonlinear Reynolds stress feedback is strongly modified by the actuation.
hypotheses.code_reuse: ADAPT (Repurpose W9-G resolvent SVD module to output wall-gain transfer matrix)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Compute resolvent gain for spanwise wall oscillation at omega=0.05. Predict wall shear reduction and compare against 5-step DNS truth run with wall actuation. If predicted gain does not correlate with measured shear reduction (correlation < 0.7), hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Determines whether our resolvent infrastructure accurately identifies optimal drag-reduction control frequencies without requiring full-field ROM simulation.

hypotheses.name: On-the-Fly Pseudospectral Evaluator for General Quadratic Conservation Laws (MHD / Burgers)
hypotheses.original_failure: Method succeeded completely in W7 (cut memory from 131 MB to 0.45 MB), but was only evaluated on periodic Navier-Stokes.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Evaluates quadratic modal interactions <phi_k, (u·∇)v> on-the-fly via 3D real FFTs without pre-storing or contracting sparse triad tensors Q_kij.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: 1D/2D/3D Burgers equation, shallow-water equations, and Incompressible Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) induction equations (u·∇)B and (B·∇)u.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (MHD induction and Lorentz force have identical quadratic momentum advection structure: curl(u x B) = (B·∇)u - (u·∇)B for solenoidal fields).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: ESTABLISHED (Orszag 1971, Stud. Appl. Math.; Canuto et al. 2006, Spectral Methods)
hypotheses.novelty: ALREADY STANDARD (Standard spectral technique; high implementation value for multi-field extensions)
hypotheses.important_differences: MHD has two coupled solenoidal vector fields (velocity u and magnetic field B); total system size is 2x larger.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: The pseudospectral evaluation algorithm operates component-wise: 3D FFT -> physical product -> inverse 3D FFT. It generalizes trivially to cross-field products u x B with exact discrete dealiasing.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: High magnetic Reynolds number (Rm) flows develop thin current sheets that may require adaptive dealiasing or higher spectral resolution than pure hydrodynamic flow.
hypotheses.code_reuse: ADAPT (Wrap OntheFlyFFTEvaluator to accept two vector fields u and B)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Implement 1D viscous Burgers equation u_t + u*u_x = nu*u_xx with OntheFlyFFTEvaluator. Compare execution time and memory against explicit triad tensor contraction for N=256 modes. If FFT is slower or memory exceeds 1 MB, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Measures crossover mode count where on-the-fly FFT outperforms tensor storage for arbitrary 1D/2D quadratic systems.

hypotheses.name: Solenoidal Vector Basis for Incompressible Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) & Kinematic Dynamo
hypotheses.original_failure: Full-state turbulent velocity compression plateaued at ~24% error with global Fourier modes.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Constructs vector modal bases that satisfy exact discrete divergence-free constraints (div B = 0) to machine precision without requiring magnetic pressure/potential Poisson solves.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Kinematic dynamo simulations and incompressible MHD reduced-order modeling.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Magnetic field B satisfies div B = 0 identically by Gauss's law for magnetism. Induction equation B_t = curl(u x B) + eta * Lap(B) preserves solenoidality).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (Dudley & James 1989, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A; Roberts 1972, Philos. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN COMPONENTS / NEW COMBINATION (Applying our exact staggered-grid solenoidal basis to kinematic magnetic field induction)
hypotheses.important_differences: In kinematic dynamo, velocity field u is prescribed (e.g. Roberts flow or ABC flow), making the magnetic induction equation linear in B.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: Because kinematic dynamo is linear in B, modal induction equations are exact and have no closure problem. Divergence-free basis eliminates the notorious numerical div(B) monopole accumulation errors in standard CFD/MHD codes.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: If the chosen velocity field generates singular magnetic flux ropes that require localized rather than global Fourier basis representation.
hypotheses.code_reuse: DIRECT (Instantiate FourierSolenoidalBasis for magnetic field B; prescribe velocity u)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Run Roberts cellular flow kinematic dynamo with FourierSolenoidalBasis at magnetic Reynolds number Rm=10. Measure magnetic growth rate gamma. If divergence norm ||div B|| > 1e-12 or gamma differs from Roberts analytical value by >1%, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Decisively proves whether our solenoidal basis framework solves the kinematic dynamo eigenvalue problem exactly without magnetic divergence cleaning.

hypotheses.name: Clustered Local POD for Multi-Regime Nonlinear Vibrations and Snap-Through Buckling
hypotheses.original_failure: Not extensively tested for turbulent channel flow because turbulence on a continuous attractor has uncountably many states rather than discrete well-separated clusters.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: K-means state-space clustering of simulation snapshots and construction of specialized local POD subspaces with online nearest-cluster projection switching.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Structural mechanics systems with multiple discrete equilibria, such as bistable arched beams exhibiting snap-through buckling or multi-mode nonlinear aeroelastic flutter.
hypotheses.structural_match: HIGH (Bistable buckling dynamics naturally inhabit two localized basins of attraction connected by a thin transition saddle; local linear subspaces approximate the two equilibrium manifolds with high precision).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (Amsallem, Zahr, Farhat 2012, Int. J. Numer. Meth. Eng.; Kaiser et al. 2014, J. Fluid Mech.)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN BUT UNCOMMON (Applying cluster-switching POD to structural snap-through transitions)
hypotheses.important_differences: Structural system has 2-5 distinct equilibrium states, whereas turbulence has an infinite-dimensional chaotic attractor.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: Clustering is mathematically optimal when the snapshot dataset forms well-separated geometric clusters. A 2-cluster local POD can achieve <1% projection error with r=3 modes per cluster, where global POD requires r=20+ modes.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: Chattering or instability during rapid transition through the unstable saddle state between the two buckled equilibria.
hypotheses.code_reuse: DIRECT (Use ClusteredLocalPODBasis on bistable Duffing/Euler-Bernoulli beam snapshots)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Generate 100 snapshots of a 2-well Duffing oscillator undergoing chaotic snap-through. Fit 2-cluster ClusteredLocalPODBasis. If local projection error is not at least 5x lower than global 1-cluster POD at rank r=2, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Demonstrates the exact regime where clustered POD outperforms global POD by exploiting manifold multi-modality.

hypotheses.name: Divergence-Free Wavelet / Wave Packet Dictionaries for Sparse Coherent Vortex Extraction
hypotheses.original_failure: Claimed 4.85% full-field error at r=210 failed sealed reproduction in W13R-V2 (actual measured error: 63.48%).
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Construction of spatially localized, divergence-free wave-packet dictionaries and quantitative effective dimension / participation ratio analysis (SparsificationEngine).
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Inverse flow reconstruction from sparse PIV/sensor measurements and coherent vortex feature extraction (Coherent Vortex Simulation / CVS).
hypotheses.structural_match: HIGH (Coherent turbulent vortices are spatially localized tube/hairpin structures; multiscale solenoidal wave packets match the local vorticity geometry).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (Farge & Schneider 2001, Phys. Fluids; Deriaz & Perrier 2006, J. Turbul.)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN COMPONENTS / NEW COMBINATION (Using our discrete MAC-staggered wave packet generator for sparse sensor reconstruction)
hypotheses.important_differences: Goal is static field denoising and sparse identification of vortex cores, NOT forward dynamical time-stepping.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: Wavelet thresholding decomposes turbulent fields into sparse non-Gaussian coherent structures (compressible in wavelets) and Gaussian background noise. Our NonorthogonalProjectionSolver can extract these structures via greedy pursuit.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: If the dictionary construction lacks sufficient directional orientational selectivity (e.g. requires 3D curvelets/shearlets rather than separable tensor products).
hypotheses.code_reuse: ADAPT (Combine W13-G wave packet generator with greedy pursuit reconstruction)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Embed a synthetic localized Hill's spherical vortex into random Gaussian noise on a 32^3 grid. Reconstruct from 50 random point samples using W13-G dictionary + NonorthogonalProjectionSolver. If reconstructed vortex position error > 2 grid cells, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Clarifies whether our multiresolution solenoidal dictionary has genuine localized feature detection capability when decoupled from the failed W13-G full-state capacity claim.

hypotheses.name: Separable Channel Eigenbasis for Acoustic Wave Propagation & Duct Resonators
hypotheses.original_failure: Limited to ~25% error on turbulent flow fields due to wide turbulent broadband spectrum.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Tensor-product basis construction exploiting 2D periodic homogeneous directions (x, z) combined with analytical wall-normal boundary eigenfunctions in inhomogeneous direction y.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Acoustic Helmholtz resonance, duct acoustics, and sound propagation in rectangular HVAC/turbomachinery ducts with impedance walls.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Acoustic wave equation in rectangular ducts has identical tensor-product Helmholtz operator (Lap + k_0^2) p = 0 with hard/soft wall boundary conditions).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: ESTABLISHED (Morse & Ingard 1968, Theoretical Acoustics; Rienstra & Hirschberg 2004, An Introduction to Acoustics)
hypotheses.novelty: ALREADY STANDARD (Standard acoustic modal expansion; high direct applicability)
hypotheses.important_differences: Acoustic wave propagation is governed by the linear wave/Helmholtz equation (scalar pressure p) rather than nonlinear vector Navier-Stokes.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: For linear acoustic ducts, the separable eigenmodes are EXACT duct modes (cut-on and cut-off acoustic modes). Broadband sound transmission is represented to machine precision with low rank.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: Only if ducts have non-rectangular cross-sections or complex acoustic liners with frequency-dependent impedance boundary conditions.
hypotheses.code_reuse: DIRECT (Apply SeparableChannelEigenbasis to scalar acoustic pressure wave equation)
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Simulate broadband acoustic pulse propagating down a 3D rectangular duct with rigid walls. Compare modal reconstruction against analytical modal cut-on dispersion relation. If dispersion error > 0.1%, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Validates exact acoustic duct mode propagation and demonstrates cross-domain transfer to engineering aeroacoustics.

hypotheses.name: Grassmannian Subspace Tracking for Neural Network Representation Stability Analysis
hypotheses.original_failure: W4 was a diagnostic tool that explained why POD failed (distance > 1.5), rather than a solver itself.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Computes exact Grassmannian chordal distance, principal angles, and cross-Gramian SVD between two arbitrary linear subspaces.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Monitoring representation drift, layer weight alignment, and mode collapse during deep neural network training (e.g. tracking subspace spanned by top singular vectors of weight matrices across epochs).
hypotheses.structural_match: HIGH (Weight matrix representations in neural networks form linear subspaces in activation space; Grassmannian distance quantifies representation alignment independently of coordinate rotations).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (Raghu et al. 2017, NeurIPS — SVCCA; Kornblith et al. 2019, ICML — CKA / Similarity of Neural Network Representations)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN BUT UNCOMMON (Applying our exact cross-Gram SVD tools to neural network representation tracking)
hypotheses.important_differences: Neural network weight matrices are dense and have dimensions (e.g. 512 x 512) rather than discretized grid fields.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: Our subspace_distance_metric computes the exact Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) / Grassmannian principal angles used in modern ML interpretability tools.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: Standard ML tools (e.g. PyTorch SVCCA packages) already exist; our implementation is in NumPy and tailored to CFD data structures.
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Compute subspace distance between weight matrices of a 3-layer MLP trained on MNIST with 2 different random initializations. If distance is identically 1.0 (no correlation detected) across all layers, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Evaluates utility of our Grassmannian metric as an ML interpretability tool.

hypotheses.name: Scientific Evidence Bundle & Metric Hashing for General Benchmark Reproducibility
hypotheses.original_method: EvidenceBundle, LockManagerV2, audit_recompute, and Metric Oracle (Audit Infrastructure)
hypotheses.original_failure: No failure; the infrastructure successfully caught multiple historical metric discrepancies, prevented hardcoded fabrication, and enforced sealed reproducibility across W12-W13R-V2.
hypotheses.demonstrated_capability: Write-once SHA256 directory hashing, Python metric source-code inspection/hashing, independent automated recomputation from raw arrays, and tamper detection.
hypotheses.candidate_problem: Reproducibility, data provenance, and automated tamper-proofing in scientific computing benchmarks, machine learning leaderboards, and computational engineering pipelines.
hypotheses.structural_match: VERY HIGH (Completely domain-agnostic software architecture: operates on file paths, JSON manifests, and NumPy `.npy` arrays).
hypotheses.literature_precedent: STRONG PRECEDENT (Peng 2011, Science — Reproducible Research in Computational Science; Stodden et al. 2016, Science — Enhancing Reproducibility)
hypotheses.novelty: KNOWN COMPONENTS / NEW COMBINATION (Combining cryptographic code hashing, write-once filesystem semantics, and AST metric function hashing into a lightweight Python package)
hypotheses.important_differences: None. The software has zero CFD-specific mathematical assumptions.
hypotheses.why_it_may_work: The audit infrastructure is fully decoupled from the Navier-Stokes equations; it can wrap any Python simulation, optimization, or ML benchmark.
hypotheses.why_it_may_fail: If large-scale distributed runs generate petabytes of raw data where full-array hashing becomes I/O bound (mitigated by streaming chunked hashes).
hypotheses.cheapest_falsification: Wrap a non-fluid benchmark (e.g. Scikit-learn classifier training) in EvidenceBundle. Mutate one entry in the raw predictions array. Run audit_recompute. If tamper detection fails to flag the mutation, hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.expected_information: Demonstrates immediate, zero-friction packaging of our audit infrastructure for general scientific computing.
